the metabolic rates of human knee joint tissues can be measured non-invasively in vivo, that these rates are elevated in rheumatoid knees, and that the metabolic and circulatory changes in the joint are responsive to synovectomy and intra-articular corticosteoroid injection.
the oxygen consumption rate and lactate production rate are increased in rheumatoid joints compared with control knees.
the metabolic rate of the rheumatoid joint is 2-3 times greater than that of normal joint and that the rheumatoid synovium is a metabolically active tissue.

the measurement of the metabolic activity of the human knee joint.
the assessment of disease severity in rheumatoid synovitis by the measurement of joint metabolism and joint circulation in vivo.

the development of a method for the assessment of the metabolic status of the human knee joint and the application of this method for the assessment and monitoring of disease activity in patients with rheumatid arthritis.

the metabolic approach described in this paper is useful for the study of knee joint metabolism.

the metabolic rate of a joint is a function of its blood supply and metabolic demand.
